pass_a_gloss: [...] should we bring up thank-offering songs? I then am, and there is not yet [another]. For if he himself is the one who made the heaven and showed forth the earth, and made it not for empty, but to be inhabited, who else would be understood as being God beside him? Or who would weigh equal to him in strength and glory? Or who at all near and by a little? And how is not the whole nature of the things that came to be defeated by the glory, strength and wisdom so great and surpassing all things? There is none. Alone then, and wholly no other upon him, would he be understood to be God by nature and truly. But yes, someone might say sometimes: Who knew the aim in him? Or who is the one able to tell whether ever he wishes also some others to be crowned with the glory and calling of God, or himself and alone? So he makes defence and says: Not in secret have I spoken, nor in a dark place of earth; I did not say to the seed of Jacob: Seek vain things. Laws, he says, I appointed for them about these things, not speaking in a corner, nor eager to escape notice, but clearly and openly. For the Lord came down upon the mountain Sinai in form of fire; there was gloom and storm and smokes, and sound of trumpets piercing. For all the people stood by, Moses acting as mediator, and laws were proclaimed from God, not charging Israel to seek something vain, that is, an idol, or a falsely named reverence, but on the contrary commandments keeping away. For it has been said to him: You will worship the Lord your God, and him alone you will serve, and there will not be for you other gods except me. And you will not make for yourself an idol, nor likeness of anything, as many as in the heaven above, and as many as in the earth below, and as many as in the waters under the earth. So it has been said to him; and the 'I am the Lord', similar as if he should say, and not once, very many times, that indeed I alone am God and Lord of all, speaking righteousness and announcing truth; and righteousness, as I think, he says the law; for the law is arbiter of righteousness; and truth the teachings of Christ. And there is in the law the outline of the truth, and the mystery of Christ has been hidden in the shadows. For Moses wrote about him. So in speaking the righteousness, the power of the truth is announced with it, if indeed it is true that the law was a shadow, and now in it the outline of the truth. [Lemma, Isaiah 45:20:] Be gathered, and come, take counsel together, those being saved from the nations. They did not know, those lifting the wood, their carving, and praying as to gods, who do not save. The apostate dragon led astray from the close kinship toward God those being on the earth, and [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: …should we offer up songs of thanksgiving? “I am, then, and there is no other” (Isaiah 45:18). For if He it is who made the heaven, who showed forth the earth and did not make it for nothing but to be inhabited, who else could be thought to be God besides Him? Or who could equal Him in strength and glory? Or who could come near Him at all, even by a little? And how is the whole nature of created things not surpassed by a glory, strength and wisdom so great and so far above all things? There is no one. He alone, then, and no other at all besides Him, could be thought to be God by nature and in truth.

Yes, but someone might perhaps say: “Who has known His purpose in this? Or who can tell whether He wishes some others also to be crowned with the glory and the name of God, or Himself alone?” So He answers this and says: “I have not spoken in secret, nor in a dark place of the earth; I did not say to the offspring of Jacob, ‘Seek vain things’” (Isaiah 45:19). I laid down laws for them about these things, He says, not speaking in a corner or trying to escape notice, but clearly and openly.

For the Lord came down on Mount Sinai in the form of fire; there was darkness and storm and smoke, and the piercing sound of trumpets (Exodus 19:16-19; Hebrews 12:18-19). The whole people stood by, with Moses acting as mediator, and laws were proclaimed from God. He did not charge Israel to seek anything vain, that is, an idol or a falsely named object of worship; on the contrary, the commandments kept them from such things. For it was said to him: “You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him alone shall you serve (Matthew 4:10; Deuteronomy 6:13); and you shall have no other gods besides Me. And you shall not make for yourself an idol, nor the likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth” (Exodus 20:3-4).

So it was said to him. And the words “I am the Lord” are as if He were saying, not once but many times over, “I alone am God and Lord of all, speaking righteousness and declaring truth” (Isaiah 45:19). By righteousness, I think, He means the Law, for the Law is the arbiter of righteousness; and by truth, the teachings of Christ. Yet the outline of the truth is present in the Law (Romans 2:20), and the mystery of Christ lies hidden in its shadows; for Moses wrote about Him (John 5:46). So in speaking righteousness, the power of the truth is also declared along with it, since it is true that the Law was a shadow (Hebrews 10:1), and that in it now lies the outline of the truth.

“Gather together and come, take counsel together, you who are being saved from the nations. Those who carry the wood, their carved image, did not know, and they pray as to gods that do not save” (Isaiah 45:20).

choices.term: τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ δόξης καὶ κλήσει
choices.english: the glory and the name of God
choices.why: κλῆσις is the name 'God', not a calling.
παράβυστος, a hidden corner; God gave the Law openly at Sinai.
Romans 2:20: the Law holds the outline of the truth, which Christ fulfils.
ἀποβουκολέω, to lead cattle astray; the devil lures people from God.
